note: From the 2026-08-03 research pass. Leads failed only our evidence bar or the count; blocked can never ship.

leads.name: Milestone Hackberry of the Todai-ji West Gate
leads.why: 3.95m girth and 30m, the tallest tree in the official Nara Park giant-tree course, believed to mark the milestone on the Kyoto road that begins at Todai-ji's Tegai-mon. Age explicitly not recorded, single official source, and no coordinate exists for the West Gate ruins in any gazetteer. Needs a pin before it can ship. CHECKED AGAIN 2026-08-14 (verify pass): confirmed the source is the Ministry of the Environment's own giant-tree database (kyoju.biodic.go.jp, both the illustrated English course PDF at kyoju.biodic.go.jp/files/course/001/guide_narakouen_en.pdf and the Japanese course page, _command=modelCourse001), an official government register, so it counts as one source. Could NOT find an independent second source: several WebSearch summaries claimed a prefectural natural monument designation, but a direct fetch of Nara City's own designated-monument list (city.nara.lg.jp/site/bunkazai/2460.html) does NOT include this tree, so that designation claim does not hold up and must not be repeated. No blog, society survey (checked kyoboku.jp's Nara Park page) or second register turned it up. The historical Todaiji West Gate ruin site itself has a documented address (406-1 Zoshi-cho, same as the temple generally) but no tree-level coordinate. Still needs: one more independent source for existence/species, and a coordinate (satellite/aerial identification of the ruin mound, which the government PDF's course map places just west of Todaiji-nandaimon Gate near Mitoriiike pond, between Isuien Garden and the Nara Prefectural Museum).

leads.name: Roben-sugi at Nigatsu-do [RESOLVED 2026-08-14, delivered as nra_010]
leads.why: Superb legend: the infant Roben was said to have been carried off by an eagle and left in its branches, and Todai-ji's founding abbot was reunited with his mother beneath it. Confirmed 2026-08-14 across four independent sources (jinja-tera-gosyuin-meguri.com, naratrip.com, gururinkansai.com, data.japanmystery.com): the original tree lived roughly 600 years and stood ~21.2m before the Second Muroto Typhoon destroyed it on 16 September 1961; sources disagree on the exact generation count since (third vs fourth planting) but agree the present tree is a replanting roughly six decades old. Delivered to data/research/nara-verified.json as nra_010, location_precision approximate (shrine-level: below the Nigatsu-do slope, north of Kojo Shrine), story must say plainly it is a replanting.

leads.name: Wakamiya Great Camphor, Kasuga Taisha
leads.why: Legend says Empress Jingu planted it. Sources contradict badly on size: 12.46m girth and 24m in one record against '8m+, 7m tall, three trees planted together' in another, which is not a rounding difference. No official register lists it, and the one open photo fails the card crop with stone lanterns filling the centre. CHECKED AGAIN 2026-08-14 (verify pass): a WebSearch summary surfaced a THIRD figure, 11.46m girth and 24m height, calling it 'one of the top 1-2 largest trees in Nara Prefecture' and giving the alternate name 'Chitose Kusu' (千歳楠); could not trace this to a specific fetchable page to confirm it independently, and it does not resolve the existing conflict, it deepens it (three different girths now: 12.46m, 11.46m, and 8m+). Also confirmed via direct fetch of narashikanko.or.jp and kasugataisha.or.jp/en pages that the well-documented '8.7m girth, 25m, 800-1000 years' figure circulating in search results belongs to the Great Cedar (Shato-no-Ohsugi, already published as nra_002), not this camphor; that mix-up is why the size kept looking resolvable and wasn't. Do not ship until a single fetchable, citable source can be pinned down for one girth figure; this is now a three-way conflict, not two-way.

leads.name: The Cedar of the Shrine Path near Nigatsu-do
leads.why: RETIRED 2026-09-08, one day after publication. Published from a reader's photograph with ZERO verified sources, against the standing bar of two independent sources for existence, species and age. The run applied 'publish and ask' (2026-08-13), which covers an empty FIELD on a tree that clears the bar, not the question of whether the tree clears it at all. Each story argued against its own inclusion: the Nigatsu-do slope 'holds cedars like this by the dozen', the pond could not be named, the temple behind the wall could not be established. Nothing here is wrong about the trees; they are simply not established as remarkable, which is what a city page promises. Everything is kept: the photograph, the coordinate and the full story. Goes back the day a source names one.
leads.story:
Ninety-nine metres from Nigatsu-do's famous Roben-sugi stands a second cedar nobody has named. A reader photographed it beside a small shrine building on the same forested slope, in the cluster of guardian sub-shrines, Kojo-sha, Iimichi-jinja and Onyu-jinja among them, that share this stretch of Todai-ji's outer precinct.

The trunk is buttressed and straight, old enough to belong here rather than beside it, and its crown forks the way a cedar's does once it has stopped competing for height with the pines around it. The old-growth forest around Nigatsu-do holds cedars like this by the dozen, most with no individual record at all: land this old accumulates trees faster than anyone can catalogue them.

We could not match this one to any of the three named sub-shrines, or find a register entry for a cedar at this exact spot, so nothing here has an age or a girth. What we have is a photograph, a coordinate and a species that is not in doubt.

If you know which shrine this stands beside, or have stood in front of it yourself, tell us. Todai-ji's precinct is free and open, the same ground as the Roben-sugi a short walk away.
leads.access: Free, open ground within Todai-ji's outer Nigatsu-do precinct, the same forested slope as the Roben-sugi

leads.story:
This cedar leans hard over the gravel road climbing toward Nigatsu-do, close enough to the power lines strung across it that whoever put them up clearly decided the tree was staying. A reader's photograph is the only record of it: no register, no temple page, no name.

Todai-ji's Nigatsu-do hillside is old forest rather than a planted garden, and it holds cedars like this in numbers nobody has individually catalogued, unlike the Roben-sugi eighty-nine metres away, which earned its name from a legend rather than its age. This one has no legend attached, just a lean pronounced enough to notice from the road and a trunk old enough to have outlasted whatever once grew beside it and left it leaning that way.

Species is certain from the bark and foliage in the photograph. Age, girth and name are not recorded anywhere we could find in the time we had to look.

The whole hillside is open, free ground, part of Todai-ji's outer precinct. If you know this tree by name, or can say why it leans the way it does, we would like to hear it.
leads.access: Free, open ground beside a gravel road within Todai-ji's outer precinct

leads.story:
A reader's photograph places a broad, dense-crowned tree beside a wooden rest pavilion and a small pond somewhere in the open ground between Todai-ji and Kasuga Taisha, part of Nara Park's Kasugano stretch. Several ponds sit in this area, Kagami-ike among the named ones, and none lines up exactly with the coordinate the phone recorded, so this entry cannot say which one.

The crown shape and leaf density suggest a mature zelkova, one of the more common large park trees in Nara, but the photograph does not show the bark or leaf edges clearly enough to be sure, so the species stays a guess rather than a claim.

What is certain is that a real tree stands there: broad-canopied, mature, shading a pavilion that people clearly use to rest. Nara Park carries no fences or opening hours across this whole stretch, so whatever it turns out to be, anyone can walk up to it today.

If you know this spot, the name of the pond or the pavilion would place it precisely, and the species would settle the rest.
leads.access: Free, open parkland; this stretch of Nara Park between Todai-ji and Kasuga Taisha has no fences or opening hours

leads.story:
A ginkgo with a heavily fluted, multi-stemmed base grows beside a long plastered wall with the tiled coping of a temple precinct, on a small street of shops and houses a few minutes walk from Todai-ji's southern approach. A second ginkgo of the same size stands further along the same wall in the reader's photograph, which is the only record either tree has.

Ginkgo is not in doubt from the fan-shaped leaves, but which temple the wall belongs to is: nothing we could find names a great ginkgo on this street, and the shopfronts around it carry no sign of what lies behind the wall. Whatever the answer, the tree itself stands in view from the pavement, which is where the photograph was taken.

Age, girth and the temple's name are all missing from this entry, which is unusual for a tree this size and this obviously old. If you know this street, a few hundred metres north of Kofuku-ji in Nara, the missing name is probably one sentence away.
leads.access: Visible from the public street; which temple's grounds lie behind the wall is not established

leads.name: The Cedars of Mizukoshi Shrine
leads.why: NARA-KYOJU PASS 2026-09-08. Well-verified otherwise: Nara City-designated natural monument (1985-03-07, 'Mizukoshi Jinja Shasou'), giant cedars up to 650cm girth (register report_id 47042, matched independently by hitozato-kyoboku.com citing the Ministry of Environment's own 2000 survey), 300+ years, standing paired either side of the shrine building at Oji-cho near the Nunome Dam. Three sources: kyoju.biodic.go.jp/?_action=gtsearchdetail&report_id=47042&branch_number=1, city.nara.lg.jp/site/bunkazai/8379.html, hitozato-kyoboku.com/mizukoshijinja-sugi.htm. BLOCKED for distance, matching the precedent this file already applies to Takiyama (Tsuge-Hayama-cho, 'far over 30 minutes out') and Shoryaku-ji (Bodaisen-cho): Nara Kotsu bus route 94/102 from Kintetsu Nara Station to the Oji-Nakamura stop alone runs 53 to 59 minutes, then about a 25-minute walk to the shrine, well over an hour each way and nothing like the rest of Nara's cluster around Nara Park. Also note for whoever revisits this: the raw register carried 8 rows for this shrine that resolve to at most 3 to 4 living cedars (near-duplicate girths pairing 650~633, 580~570, 555~550, 520~520, almost certainly two ministry survey passes over the same trees), and hitozato-kyoboku's 2023 visit notes that one of the four originally registered cedars had already died and been removed by 2004 (stump and a marker post remain), so do not ship all 8 rows as separate trees if this is ever revisited. Worth keeping as a lead in case Oji-cho or the wider Yagyu/Nunome Dam area is ever treated as its own place rather than folded into the Nara city page.

leads.name: Shimobe Shrine cedars and ginkgo
leads.why: NARA-KYOJU PASS 2026-09-08. 9 register rows (cedars 307-450cm, one ginkgo 327cm), none carrying an official designation (desig=なし throughout), ages 100-299 years. Facility is 下部神社 (Shimobe Shrine), address 奈良県奈良市都祁吐山町 (Tsuge-Hayama-cho) per Yahoo Map / Mapion listings. This is the SAME hamlet already blocked in this file for the Takiyama left-spiral Torreya ('inside the municipal boundary only through a merger and far over 30 minutes out'), roughly 6km north of Haibara/Sakurai and nowhere near Nara Park. Not independently re-timed this pass; blocked on the strength of the existing Takiyama precedent for the identical place name. Not designated, so even setting distance aside these would need a second source before shipping.

leads.name: Yagyu Yamaguchi Shrine cedars
leads.why: NARA-KYOJU PASS 2026-09-08. 5 register rows, girths 377cm to 540cm, ages 200 to 300+ years, no official designation. Facility is 夜支布山口神社 (Yagyu Yamaguchi Shrine), in the Yagyu district, a mountain hamlet in eastern Nara City historically associated with the Yagyu swordsman clan, roughly 12 to 16km from central Nara by road. Distance not independently timed this pass (unlike Mizukoshi and Shimobe above), so left as a lead rather than blocked outright, but expect the same day-trip problem: check Nara Kotsu bus timetables to Yagyu before spending more research time here, and note no designation was found for any of these five trees, so a second source is also needed regardless of distance.

leads.name: Kasuga Taisha's other giant trees (ginkgo, deer park camphor)
leads.why: NARA-KYOJU PASS 2026-09-08. Two candidates at the already-published Kasuga Taisha precinct, distinct from the Great Cedar (nra_002) and Great Nagi (nra_006) already live: (1) a 430cm ginkgo at the main shrine (register report_id 47074, no designation); (2) a 462cm camphor at Kasuga Taisha's Rokuen deer park (report_id 47077, NATIONALLY designated as a monument per the register, Rokuen itself confirmed open to visitors per narashikanko.or.jp/en/spot/park/rokuen/). Neither tree could be matched to an independent second source this pass: kasugataisha.or.jp's own 'forest walk' pages (guidance/morisanpo/ and morisanpo2/) hang on curl (exit 28, full 20s timeout, both attempts) and were not reachable via WebFetch either this pass; general search results confirm Kasuga Taisha has '33 giant trees over 3m girth' city-designated as of March 2019 but none of the summaries named this specific ginkgo or this specific camphor. Worth a dedicated pass that can get past the kasugataisha.or.jp hang (try Wayback Machine snapshots of guidance/morisanpo2/, per this project's standing playbook for hanging hosts).

leads.name: Todai-ji's other designated trees (Aragashi, Konara)
leads.why: NARA-KYOJU PASS 2026-09-08. Two candidates at the already-published Todai-ji precinct, distinct from the Chinaberry (nra_008, matches register report_id 47081) already live: (1) an Arakashi (Japanese blue oak) at 365cm, PREFECTURALLY designated plus urban-park designated (report_id 47082); (2) a Konara oak at 302cm, NATIONALLY plus prefecturally designated (report_id 47080), but the register itself flags visibility as 'cannot be confirmed without approaching', i.e. tucked away. Real official designations on both, but no independent second source turned up this pass beyond the register and the ministry's own Nara Park course guide PDF (kyoju.biodic.go.jp/files/course/001/guide_narakouen_ja.pdf, already used for nra_005/006/008/009, arguably not fully independent of the register itself; the PDF could not be parsed this pass, no PDF text tool available in this environment). Worth a dedicated pass with PDF tooling or a Japanese Wikipedia / prefecture cultural-property page check.

leads.name: Toshodai-ji's camphor at Mizukagami Shrine
leads.why: NARA-KYOJU PASS 2026-09-08. 360cm camphor (register report_id 47058), facility named 唐招提寺内水鏡社 ('within Toshodai-ji, at Mizukagami Shrine'). Toshodai-ji is one of Nara's major UNESCO World Heritage temples, not currently represented on our city page at all, so a good tree here would be a genuinely new site. Confirmed Mizukagami (Tenjin) Shrine is real: historically Toshodai-ji's own guardian shrine, separated from the temple administratively in the Meiji shinbutsu-bunri reforms but still managed by the temple today (ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/唐招提寺). Could not find any source, dedicated or general, naming a specific giant camphor there; age unknown even in the register (health/age fields largely blank for this row). Needs a dedicated look, ideally with a source that can be fetched (toshodaiji.jp itself was not tried this pass).

leads.name: Byakugo-ji's second tree (Zelkova)
leads.why: NARA-KYOJU PASS 2026-09-08. 310cm Zelkova (register report_id 47053, age unrecorded, no designation), at the same temple as the already-published Five-Colour Camellia (nra_003). No independent source found naming this tree; Byakugo-ji's own coverage (narashikanko.or.jp, yamatoji.nara-kankou.or.jp) discusses the camellia and the temple's autumn bush clover but not a zelkova. Low priority: no designation, no second source, and a temple already represented by its more famous camellia.

leads.name: Sugawara-area shrines (Tenmangu and Sugawara Shrine trees)
leads.species: mixed: Cryptomeria japonica, Quercus glauca, Zelkova serrata, Torreya nucifera, Celtis sinensis, Cinnamomum camphora, Quercus myrsinifolia
leads.why: NARA-KYOJU PASS 2026-09-08. Two related facility names in the register, likely the same precinct or adjacent sites in west Nara: 天満宮 (8 rows, girths 300 to 455cm, ages 100 to 300+ years, no designation) and 菅原神社 (2 rows, camphor 300cm and hackberry 323cm, no designation). Best guess is Sugawara Tenmangu (菅原天満宮), described by its own site (sugawaratenmangu.com) and Wikipedia as Japan's oldest Tenmangu shrine, in Sugawara-Higashi, west Nara, well within the city's usual reach. Not confirmed against the register rows: could not find any source describing individual giant trees on the grounds, and with two similarly-named facilities in the raw data this needs a geocoding pass before anything can be pinned, let alone sourced. None of the 10 rows carry an official designation. Deprioritise unless a dedicated pass finds the naming source Nara's better-documented sites all have (per the 'does anybody NAME its trees' rule).

leads.name: Minor undesignated shrine trees (Hachioji, Hachiman, Ishiuchi, Hakusan, Jofuku-ji)
leads.species: mixed: Castanopsis cuspidata var. sieboldii, Cryptomeria japonica, Ginkgo biloba, Ilex rotunda
leads.why: NARA-KYOJU PASS 2026-09-08. Consolidated note rather than five separate stubs, all low-priority on the same grounds: 八王神社 (Tsuburajii/chinquapin, 395cm), 八幡神社 (Tsuburajii, 390cm, carries a prefectural NATURAL PARK designation, not a monument designation), 石打寺脇 and 石打人柱神社 (sugi, 378cm and 370cm), 白山神社 (ginkgo, 318cm), 淨福寺 (Ilex rotunda, 315cm). None carry a natural-monument designation, none matched to any independent source this pass, and none were geocoded. Register report_ids: 47459, 47461, 47455, 47456, 47084, 47055. Worth a look only if a dedicated pass finds a naming source for this cluster of minor shrines; otherwise not worth the token spend per tree at this evidence level.

leads.name: Private-land and no-facility register rows (nara-kyoju batch)
leads.why: NARA-KYOJU PASS 2026-09-08. Consolidated note, not itemised. 15 of the 136 rows in data/leads/nara-kyoju.json carry owner_ja='個人' (private individual): never ship per hard rule 10, skipped without further research. 73 of 136 carry no facility_ja at all and were left unresearched this pass: no name to search on, no coordinate, would need a from-zero approach outside this register-led pass's scope. 10 rows sit at 春日山原生林 (Kasugayama primeval forest), already covered by this file's existing 'Kasugayama Primeval Forest' and 'Kasuga Ichiigashi giant-tree group' blocked entries (not a collectible point); not re-added.
